newsitem.title: MALI: Sodinaf-Mali seeks $37 mln investment for gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Sodinaf-Mali seeks $37 mln investment for gold mine.

text.p: Owners of Mali's third largest gold deposit of 81 tonnes at Kodieran are seeking $37 million finance for a new mine to allow production from 1998.
Managing Director Aliou Boubacar Diallo of Sodinaf-Mali said the firm was seeking investors through Canada's Montreal stock exchange to fund mine construction.
About 22.5 million tonnes of Kodieran ore with 2.33 ounces of gold per tonne would be extracted over a period of eight years, he told Reuters.
"(The reserves) mean for us production of three tonnes of gold in the first year," he said, adding that production would rise to five tonnes from 1999.
The Kodieran mine, part of the Ouassoulou gold region, would be built by Canadian firm Roche. Diallo said Roche completed reserve assessment and recovery feasibility studies at Kodieran in late 1996.
He said Roche had proposed a gravitational gold recovery technique which would avoid the need for heap-leaching -- soaking piles of gold ore with environmentally toxic diluted cyanide-based products.

Gold mining has expanded rapidly in Mali and other African countries since 1990 as governments have opened mining to foreign investment. Sodinaf-Mali is a privately owned Malian holding company set up in 1993.
Diallo said mining had a certain future in Mali, "...on condition that operators accept constraints which require patience and sometimes investments at a loss."
Mali's two largest known gold deposits are already being mined by South African owners as other firms continue with exploration projects.
Randgold is mining one of West Africa's largest mine sites at Syama in western Mali, producing six tonnes a year.

Mali's largest mine at Sadiola, with reserves of 141 tonnes of gold, producing around 10 tonnes a year, is owned by South Africa's Anglo-American Corp. Sodinaf-Mali also bought mining rights at Wala, near Sadiola, in 1996. --Abidjan newsroom + 21 90 90
